document.title: Eval: grade with Ember, keep the Spark producer
document.summary: Ember grades eval reviews by default; the producer stays on Spark contributor, and non-contributor models now run on the subscription.
document.why: Evals spend the Muse Code subscription by default, so each seat should use the cheapest model that keeps quality on that billing path.

sources.title: Eval: grade with Ember, keep the Spark producer
sources.gist: Measured Ember against Spark contributor in both seats; grader switches, producer stays.

groups.title: Contributor mode per model
groups.summary: A new contributorMode helper passes contributor mode on only for muse-spark contributor variants and off for other models, so Ember and Wonder run on the subscription instead of failing.

commits.subject: Eval: grade with Ember by default, keep Spark producer
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Repeated rescores put Ember at Spark parity on verdicts and tokens
at 3.7x the speed. Producer spot checks stay thinner on Ember.

commits.subject: Eval: pass contributor-mode off for non-contributor models
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Ember has no contributor variant and rejects contributor mode on,
on the subscription too. Pass on only for muse-spark contributor
tiers. Docs record the corrected Ember verdict.

commits.subject: Eval docs: say per 1M tokens on both Ember tiers
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Eval docs: give both Ember price tiers
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Eval: record why Ember does not replace Spark contributor
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Ember has no contributor variant, is absent from the Muse Code
subscription login, and costs more per output token on the Model API.
Grader agreement was near parity in rescore checks. Keep defaults.
